chapter: Los Angeles: Roy Milton and Central Avenue
title: After-hours places along San Pedro
summary: Casablanca, Cafe Society, Big Jim Wynn, and other late places on San Pedro, with Red Mack and Tom Archia.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: And then they had plenty of after-hour places, like the Casablanca over on San Pedro. After-hours was anything that was open after two o'clock, because as it is now in California, at two o'clock all the legal things shut down, you know, unless you have some kind of charter for a private club or something.
Right. It was just a gimmick for being able to stay open as long as you were greasing the right palms.

And right up the street from there was the Cafe Society, and they had a band downstairs and upstairs. They had a little trio, a very fine trio playing in there. And they also had the Trenier Twins upstairs during this period.
San Pedro, yeah. And they had another band, Jim Wynn. Big Jim Wynn and his band was playing up at the Cafe Society, playing their music over there, you know. They never...

I don't know the people who ran the Cafe Society. But then they had another little place down the street on San Pedro and Jefferson where I used to go down and play with Red Mack, the trumpet player and vibist -- we used to go in there and play with him. And Tom Archia, a very fine saxophone player from eastern Texas; I played with him the Howard McGhee band later on.
